legend: Given a positive integer sequence a1,a2,⋯,an$$$a_1, a_2, \cdots, a_n$$$ of length n$$$n$$$, you need to perform exactly k$$$k$$$ operations. For each operation, you need to choose one element and increase its value by 1$$$1$$$.
Maximize the greatest common divisor of all elements after the operations.
input: There are multiple test cases. The first line of the input contains an integer T$$$T$$$ (1≤T≤103$$$1 \le T \le 10^3$$$), indicating the number of test cases. For each test case:
The first line contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and k$$$k$$$ (1≤n≤106$$$1 \le n \le 10^6$$$, 1≤k≤1012$$$1 \le k \le 10^{12}$$$) indicating the length of the sequence and the number of operations.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,⋯,an$$$a_1, a_2, \cdots, a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤106$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^6$$$) indicating the sequence.

It's guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ of all test cases will not exceed 106$$$10^6$$$, the sum of maxai$$$\max a_i$$$ of all test cases will not exceed 106$$$10^6$$$, and the sum of k$$$k$$$ of all test cases will not exceed 1012$$$10^{12}$$$.
output: For each test case output one line containing one integer, indicating the maximum possible greatest common divisor of all elements after exactly k$$$k$$$ operations.
note: For the first sample test case, we can change the sequence to 5,10,10$$$5, 10, 10$$$, and the greatest common divisor is 5$$$5$$$.
For the second sample test case, we can change the sequence to 6,10,10$$$6, 10, 10$$$, and the greatest common divisor is 2$$$2$$$.
